price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: shot mix (play-type share, shot zone, 3PA share, rim share)
methodological_questions: Can a within-team lineup-change design detect a shift in shot mix, serving as a positive control?
How should lineup effects be separated from game state, opponent, fatigue, and coaching confounds?
Is there enough exposure per five-man unit, and is the effect measured with enough precision?
How should shot mix be measured reliably from play-by-play, and how should the positive-control success criterion be fixed in advance?

historical_evidence.finding: Shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor (N=1.07M possessions): DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (SE 0.295, t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (t=+1.1). Recorded failure evidence: sub-1pp mix shifts, chat verdict WEAK/SMALL. Limited by small sample, risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. This concerns the opponent's lineup, not the offensive five.

Opener recommendations ignored personnel: 8/8 rank-1 openers were CUT-centered and infeasible, with CUT targets 3-10x the stretch ceiling in every team-game. Failure mechanism C_artifact. Risks: BASE_RATE, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Matchup decomposition on four playoff games: team-level lifts small, player-channel lifts large on cells of n=15-54. Failure mechanism A_unanswerable; limited by insufficient exposure (EXPOSURE_SPARSITY).
Historical upset backtest on 4 series; construction or labelling flaw (C_artifact). Only tangentially relevant to this question.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Recommending team-level play-type targets without conditioning on the personnel on the floor
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the optimizer ignored personnel, so targets exceeded what the rotation could sustain.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Decomposing effects into player and play-type channels on very small cells
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: cell n of 15-54 possessions, no holdout, and primary_defender attribution that includes helper steals.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating sub-1pp shifts in rim share and PPP as a usable signal
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive: shifts were small, rim share SE 0.295, PPP t=+1.1, verdict weak/small.

evidence_establishes: A change in the opponent's on-floor personnel (SF34, inconclusive overall) was recorded with some shot-mix shifts that were individually precise at N=1.07M possessions: 3PA share -1.79pp (SE 0.31), DRIVE +0.82pp, POST_UP +0.43pp. Rim share did not move (+0.12pp, SE 0.295).
Personnel-blind approaches to play-type mix were recorded as producing artifacts (SF32).
Cell sizes of roughly 15-54 possessions were recorded as insufficient (SF-APPA-066).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five shifts shot mix: none of the retrieved records studies offensive-lineup changes.
Whether a lineup-change design works as a positive control: SF34 is the closest design and its overall status is inconclusive.
Which shot-mix measures (3PA share, rim share, play-type share) are the sensitive ones for an offensive-five contrast.
Any effect size for offensive-five changes, or the distribution of exposure across five-man units.
own_inferences: The claim is close to a tautology if the five is changed by swapping players with known different shot profiles. Shot mix is largely a function of who is shooting, so a mechanical personnel effect is almost certain, and detecting it shows little about whether the design can find non-mechanical lineup effects.

The positive control only has value if it is stated with a pre-specified direction and magnitude. For example, predict the shift from the sum of the incoming and outgoing players' own shot profiles, then test whether the observed lineup shift matches that prediction. A bare 'shot mix changed' is a weak bar.

Because the retrieved precision (SE ~0.25-0.31pp at N=1.07M) was achieved on a pooled set, the offensive-five contrast must be restricted to single-player swaps and pooled to keep similar power. Five-man units will be sparse, and many units will have too little exposure.
The SF34 3PA/DRIVE shifts have large t-values, suggesting that large-N pooled shot-mix contrasts are detectable when the contrast is pooled across many possessions.
uncertainties: Exposure per distinct five-man unit and per single-swap contrast in 2022-23 to 2024-25 has not been measured.
Whether substitution rotation intervals align exactly with play-by-play clock and possession boundaries.
Whether the question intends any change in the five or a specified type of change, and what counts as detecting an effect.
The first possessions after a substitution may reflect transitions, fatigue, dead-ball timing and set-play selection rather than the lineup itself.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior records changed the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes. SF34 shows sub-1pp shot-mix shifts can be small and inconclusive, SF32 shows personnel-blind approaches yield artifacts, and SF-APPA-066 shows small cells are unanswerable. Hence the design pools over single-player swaps, conditions on personnel, avoids tiny cells, and fixes a quantitative prediction in advance. No retrieved record answers the offensive-five question.

blocking_constraints.text: Distinct five-man units are sparse; the test must pool over single-player swaps and set minimum exposure thresholds.
Shot mix is partly defined by the shooters on the floor, so a personnel effect is close to mechanical and needs a pre-specified expected-shift benchmark.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the effect of changing the offensive five on shot mix. SF34 is the nearest design (opponent lineup, inconclusive); SF32 and SF-APPA-066 give cautionary lessons on personnel-blind targets and sparse cells.

risks.text: Swapping players with different shot profiles necessarily changes shot mix, so detection is nearly guaranteed and weakly informative about design sensitivity.
Substitutions are endogenous to score, foul trouble, fatigue, opponent lineup, period and coach intent. Lineups changed in garbage time or after timeouts differ systematically.
Many five-man units have few possessions; SF34's SEs of ~0.25-0.31pp show that sub-1pp effects need very large pooled N.
Cell sizes of 15-54 were unanswerable in SF-APPA-066; per-unit and per-swap cells may be similarly thin.
Shot mix as measured includes the shooters' own tendencies; play-type labels derived from play-by-play may encode who the initiator is.
Shot-zone and play-type shares are noisy in short stints; derived play-type possession records may misclassify.
Multiple shot-mix measures (3PA, rim, DRIVE, POST_UP, PPP) invite selective reporting; SF34 reported several with mixed results.
Style and rule changes across 2022-25 and between regular season and playoffs shift baseline shot mix.
Without a placebo (non-offensive personnel changes, or shuffled swap timing), a significant shift cannot be separated from time-in-game trends.

design.estimand: Within-team change in shot mix (primary: 3PA share of FGA, rim (<=4ft) share of FGA; secondary: DRIVE and POST_UP play-type share) between possessions with the outgoing five and possessions with the incoming five after a single-player substitution, compared with the shift predicted from the two players' own season-level shot profiles. The positive control passes only if (a) the observed shift has the predicted sign and (b) it correlates with the predicted shift, with a slope CI covering a pre-specified range.
design.unit: Substitution event (single-player swap) within a team-game; analysed at possession level with clustering by team-game and by swap pair.
design.sample: Regular-season and playoff games 2022-23 to 2024-25; possessions in the 10 possessions before and after each single-player swap, excluding garbage time (e.g. margin >= 20 in the 4th), end-of-period possessions, and the first possession after a timeout/dead ball. Swaps need at least N possessions per side (set at the exposure audit). Multi-player swaps are excluded from the primary analysis. 2022-23 and 2023-24 are used for tuning the exposure threshold and prediction model, 2024-25 as a holdout.
design.power: Run an exposure audit before looking at outcomes: count swaps and possessions per swap pair. Use SE benchmarks from SF34 (~0.25-0.31pp at N=1.07M possessions, pooled) to compute the minimum detectable shift; require that the pooled swap set gives SE <= 0.5pp for 3PA share. If it does not, declare untestable at that granularity rather than reduce to small cells.
design.controls: Condition on period, score margin, opponent, home/away, rest, and the outgoing player's minutes in the stint (fatigue). Use team-game fixed effects and include the opposing lineup's rim-big presence (cf. FAM:SF34). Predict the expected shift from player-level profiles estimated on data excluding the focal game (leave-game-out) to avoid circularity.
design.falsification: Placebos: (1) pseudo-substitutions at random times with no change in the five; (2) swaps in the defensive five's identity only while the offense is unchanged; (3) permuted swap labels within team-season. The design should show no shift in these. Also run a negative-control outcome unrelated to shooter identity (e.g. shot clock at shot or free-throw rate) as a check.
design.multiplicity: Two pre-registered primary outcomes (3PA share, rim share) with Holm correction; secondary outcomes (DRIVE, POST_UP, PPP) reported as exploratory with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.
design.decision_rule: Positive control declared passed if, on the 2024-25 holdout, the Holm-adjusted test shows a shift in the predicted direction for both primary outcomes, the observed-vs-predicted slope is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0, and all placebos are null at alpha=0.05. If the primary outcomes pass but placebos also move, label as artifact. If the exposure audit fails, label untestable. Do not claim that passing the control validates detection of non-mechanical lineup effects.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-02; freeze file hashes and the possession-labelling code version before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can a design detect personnel effects on shot mix as a positive control?
How should lineup-change effects on shot mix be identified given confounding by game state, opponent and coaching?
What sample size and exposure are available for five-man unit comparisons?
How is shot mix measured reliably (shot distance zones, shot type) from play-by-play?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
